chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Women do not have the right of pardon (afw) nor the right of retribution (qawd).

As for what Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Fudayl, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who pardoned a share-holder that his pardon is valid. And he ruled regarding four brothers, one of whom pardoned, saying: The remainder pays the blood money (diyah), and the one who pardoned is exempted by his share.

And what Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding two men who killed a man intentionally, and he had two heirs, and one of the heirs pardoned: He said, When some of the heirs pardon him, the killing (retribution) is removed from him, and from the two (heirs) the blood money is reduced by the share of the one who pardoned, and they pay the remainder from their wealth to the one who did not pardon. And he said: The pardon of every share-holder is valid.

Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who killed two men intentionally, and they had heirs, and the heirs of one pardoned and the other refused. He said: He kills those who did not pardon, and if they wish to take the blood money, they take it.

Abd al-Rahman said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): And two men killed a man intentionally, and he had two heirs, and one of the heirs pardoned. He said: When some of the heirs pardon him, the killing is removed from them, and from the two the blood money is reduced by the share of the one who pardoned, and they pay the remainder from their wealth to those who did not pardon.

So there is no contradiction between these narrations and the first report from two aspects: One is that it is permissible for us to specify these narrations by saying: The pardon of whoever has a share in the blood money is valid, except if he is a woman, for she does not have valid pardon nor retribution.

And the second is that these narrations only encompassed the validity of the pardon of the heirs, and the woman is not an heir (wali) of the deceased because the wali is the one who has the right to demand retribution or blood money, and the woman does not have that. And if she is not an heir, it does not contradict what we have presented.

As for what these narrations encompassed that when some of the heirs pardon, the killing is removed from him and that transfers to the blood money, the explanation is that it only transfers to the blood money if the one who wants retribution does not pay to the heirs of the one to be killed the amount that was pardoned, because if he does not pay that, he does not have retribution in any case.

And similarly the ruling regarding what 5-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghayath ibn Kalub, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever pardons the blood from a share-holder has a valid pardon, the blood is dropped and becomes blood money, and his share is removed from him. And that which indicates what we said that he has retribution if he returns the amount that was pardoned.

6-What Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man killed by a woman, and he had a father, a mother, and a son. He said: The son said: I want to kill my father's killer. The father said: I pardon. The mother said: I take the blood money. He said: So the son should give the mother of the deceased one-sixth of the blood money, and give the heirs of the killer one-sixth of the blood money, the right of the father who pardoned, and he should kill him.

7-Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of his companions, who raised it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding a man who was killed and he had two heirs, and one pardoned and the other refused to pardon. He said: The one who did not pardon, if he wishes to kill, he kills and returns half the blood money to the heirs of the deceased to be killed from him.

8-As for what Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Wallad, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man killed and he had young and adult sons. Do you see if his adult sons pardon? He said: He is not killed, and the pardon of the adults is valid in their shares. When the young ones grow up, they have the right to claim their shares from the blood money.

His saying (peace be upon him): When the young ones grow up, they have their shares from the blood money, does not indicate that they do not have retribution with the condition we mentioned. And that which indicates that they have retribution, added to what we have presented.

9-What Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghayath ibn Kalub, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) said: Wait for the young ones whose father was killed until they grow up. When they reach maturity, they are given the choice: if they wish, they kill, or pardon, or accept blood money.

key_terms.ذِي سَهْمٍ: Share-holder (one of the heirs entitled to a portion of the diyah)
key_terms.عَفْوٌ: Pardon (forgiving the right to retribution or blood money)
key_terms.قَوَدٌ: Retribution (execution of the killer in return for the victim)
key_terms.وَلِيّ: Heir/Guardian (one with the right to claim retribution or blood money)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of blood money and retribution when some heirs pardon and others do not?
ai.summary: This excerpt from al-Isfarayini's *al-Istibsar* synthesizes juristic debates on *qawd* (retribution) and *diyah* (blood money), highlighting the Shia position that women hold a share in compensation but lack the authority to pardon or execute retribution. It resolves apparent contradictions in hadith by distinguishing between the right of pardon (*afw*) and the right of retribution, while clarifying that minor heirs' pardon is provisional until they reach maturity. The text underscores the principle that partial pardon by one heir reduces the killer's liability proportionally, ensuring justice for both the pardoning and non-pardoning heirs.
